mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.25% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors seek yield in equities during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment exceeding 7.0% signals weak labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE exceeds 7.0% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous payroll growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment decline (UNRATE) indicate a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer confidence and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline occurs in 50% of periods but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of those instances.
